title: Align roles, post-login redirects, chat landing (/chat), users list (/users), chat-request flow, and admin access separation

requirements.text: Update post-login redirect logic so that after signup/login: (1) if the Firestore user profile has approved == false, navigate to /pending-approval; (2) if approved == true, ALWAYS navigate to /chat for all roles including admin and super_admin, and do not auto-redirect any admin/super_admin to /users or any admin page.

quotes: After signup/login: If approved == false → show "Pending Approval" screen. If approved == true → ALWAYS redirect to Chat Home page (/chat), even for admin or super_admin. Do NOT auto-redirect admins to User List or Admin Dashboard.

acceptanceCriteria: Given an unapproved user logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /pending-approval.
Given an approved normal user logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /chat.
Given an approved admin logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /chat.
Given an approved super_admin logs in or signs up, they are navigated to /chat.
No code path redirects users to /users based solely on role.

requirements.text: Make /chat the default landing screen for all approved users and implement the Chat Home empty state with the exact user-facing text: "Start a conversation. Tap + to find users." and a bottom-right Floating Action Button (FAB) with a plus/new-chat icon that navigates to /users when clicked.

quotes:
CHAT HOME PAGE (/chat)
- This is the default landing page for all approved users.
- Show empty-state text like:
  "Start a conversation. Tap + to find users."
- Show a Floating Action Button (FAB) at bottom-right.

FLOATING ACTION BUTTON (FAB)
- FAB icon: plus / new chat.
- On FAB click → navigate to User List page (/users).

acceptanceCriteria: When the current user has zero chats, /chat shows the empty-state text exactly: "Start a conversation. Tap + to find users."
A FAB is visible at bottom-right on /chat and uses a plus/new-chat icon.
Clicking the FAB navigates to /users.
Approved admin and approved super_admin users can access /chat and see the same chat home behavior as normal users.

requirements.text: Change /users to be a single "User List" experience for all roles that lists ALL approved users (normal, admin, and super_admin), including the currently logged-in user (do not exclude self). Each row must show the user's profile photo, name, and may show a small optional role badge.

quotes:
USER LIST PAGE (/users)
- Show ALL approved users including:
  - normal users
  - admins
  - super_admin (including the logged-in user)
- Do NOT exclude the current user.
- Each user row should show:
  - profile photo
  - name
  - role badge (optional, small)

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to /users shows a list of all approved user profiles returned by the data source, including admins and super_admins.
The currently authenticated user appears in the list.
Each list item shows avatar/photo and display name; role badge is present if implemented and is visually small/subtle.
/users no longer conditionally swaps to an admin-only user management screen based solely on role.

requirements.text: Implement the chat request UX logic on /users so that tapping a user row does NOT open a chat directly; instead it reveals a "Send Chat Request" action, and sending creates a chat_request record with fields { fromUid, toUid, status: "pending", createdAt } (preserve existing naming conventions in Firestore, but ensure these exact semantics and values).

quotes:
CHAT REQUEST LOGIC
- On tapping a user:
  - Do NOT open chat directly.
  - Show "Send Chat Request" button.
- On send request:
  - Create a chat_request document:
    { fromUid, toUid, status: "pending", createdAt }

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking/tapping a user list row does not navigate to /chat and does not open an existing chat thread.
After selecting a user, the UI presents a "Send Chat Request" button to initiate a request.

Sending a request writes a Firestore document to the chat_requests collection (or existing chat request collection) with the correct semantics: requester as fromUid, recipient as toUid, status == "pending", and createdAt populated.
The app prevents duplicate pending requests from the same sender to the same recipient (either by UI state or backend rule), without deleting or modifying existing user documents.

requirements.text: Implement request handling so the receiver is notified in the UI of incoming pending chat requests, can Accept or Reject, and: Accept creates a 1-to-1 chat thread accessible to both users; Reject does not create a chat thread. Ensure chat becomes enabled/visible for both users only after acceptance.

quotes:
REQUEST HANDLING
- Receiver sees incoming request notification.
- Receiver can Accept or Reject.
- If accepted:
  - Create a 1-to-1 chat thread.
  - Enable chat for both users.
- If rejected:
  - No chat is created.

acceptanceCriteria: When User A sends a request to User B, User B sees an incoming request UI within the app without needing a manual refresh beyond existing polling behavior.
Accepting a request creates exactly one 1-to-1 chat thread containing both user IDs and allows both users to see/open it from /chat.
Rejecting a request updates the request status appropriately and does not create any chat thread.
Users cannot send messages to each other unless there is an accepted request/chat thread.

requirements.text: Separate admin access from the normal chat flow: normal users must not see any admin dashboard/features; admin dashboard must be accessible only via the header profile dropdown item labeled "Admin Dashboard" and only visible to admin/super_admin users. Admin features must never change the post-login redirect flow or the default /chat landing behavior.

quotes:
ADMIN ACCESS (SEPARATE)
- Admin Dashboard should be accessible ONLY via:
  Header profile dropdown → "Admin Dashboard"
- Only admin/super_admin can see this option.
- Admin features must NEVER interfere with normal chat flow.

ROLES & IDENTITY
- Normal users must NOT see admin dashboard or admin features.

acceptanceCriteria: For a normal user, the header profile dropdown does not show any admin-only navigation items (including Admin Dashboard).
For an admin or super_admin, the header profile dropdown shows an "Admin Dashboard" item that navigates to the admin dashboard route.
Admin dashboard screens are guarded so only admin/super_admin can access them (direct navigation is blocked).
Approved admin/super_admin users still land on /chat after login and can use chat features without being redirected to admin areas.

requirements.text: Ensure role/identity semantics: treat super_admin as BOTH an admin and a normal user for product behavior, meaning super_admin users (and admins) must be included in the approved user list and have access to normal chat flow; normal users must not gain any admin-only capabilities.

quotes:
A super_admin is BOTH an admin and a normal user.
Admin/super_admin must appear in the user list like a normal user.
Normal users must NOT see admin dashboard or admin features.

acceptanceCriteria: super_admin users can use /chat and /users the same way as normal users (subject to approval).
Admins and super_admins appear in /users like normal users (with optional role badge).
Normal users cannot access admin routes or see admin-only UI controls.

requirements.text: Safety constraints: do not delete any existing user documents; do not modify existing user roles or approval flags as part of this change; preserve and respect the current super_admin bootstrap logic.

quotes:
IMPORTANT SAFETY
- Do NOT delete existing users.
- Do NOT change existing roles or approvals.
- Respect current super_admin bootstrap logic.

acceptanceCriteria: No migration or code path deletes user documents.
No migration or code path changes user.role or user.approved values as part of implementing the new flow (outside of existing explicit admin actions, if they remain available and guarded).
The first-user bootstrap behavior for super_admin remains unchanged.

requirements.text: Apply a cohesive, non-blue/non-purple visual theme across the updated /chat and /users experiences (colors, typography, spacing), keeping the UI consistent with the existing Tailwind + shadcn components and ensuring the FAB is visually prominent and accessible.
acceptanceCriteria: /chat and /users share a consistent visual style (typography, spacing, button styling).
The FAB meets basic accessibility expectations (keyboard focusable, visible contrast, clear hit area).

constraints: Keep all backend logic within the existing single Motoko actor (backend/main.mo); only add a migration file if state schema changes are strictly required.
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui (read-only shadcn components).
Do not edit immutable frontend paths: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx.
Use English for all user-facing text.
Do not change existing roles or approvals.
nonGoals: Implementing third-party auth providers beyond the existing Internet Identity/Firebase setup.
Adding group chats or real-time websocket-based notifications (continue using existing polling approach).
Building new admin management features beyond navigation + access separation described here.
